Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As discussed, we're kicking off an enterprise evaluation and need your completed SIG pack plus any evidence you can share around data residency, DPA/SCCs, and whether Redwood can support a BAA. High level:

- Primary use case: clinical decision support (some PII/PHI may be sent from our EHR to an integration layer).
- Expected volume: pilot 20k requests/day, potential scale later.
- Residency requirement: EEA for EU patients; US-only for US patients.

Could you: 1) share your completed SIG spreadsheet and SOC2 summary, 2) confirm whether Redwood will sign a BAA (and under what deployment model), and 3) call out what evidence we should expect for SCCs/DPA?

I've attached our filled-in SIG template for your convenience (HealthSystems_SIG_v1.xlsx).

Also cc'ing Michael (security lead) — he may have a couple of technical follow-ups.

Thanks,

Hi Claire — great to hear from you and thanks for the template.

Short answer up front: we can complete your SIG and provide SOC2 artifacts and DPA + SCCs evidence. BAA is feasible but depends on deployment: Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) or Dedicated reserved capacity with an appropriate contractual addendum are the straightforward paths for a BAA; our hosted public API can be covered in limited circumstances with additional controls and contractual language, but it's not our recommended route for production PHI.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll send our completed SIG workbook and a short evidence bundle (SOC2 summary, SCC mapping) by EOD tomorrow.
- Neha (privacy lead) and Priyom (security ops) are CC'd to answer technical/contractual questions and propose a BAA path.
- Can you confirm whether PHI will flow to the hosted public API during the pilot or whether you'll route production PHI to a Dedicated/Private deployment? That will determine timeline.

We can also set a 30-minute call to walk the packet and clarify any gaps — I'm available Thu/Fri afternoon PT.

Best,

Claire — following up with more detail from privacy/security: 

1) BAA feasibility
- Supported: Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC) and Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) — we can sign a BAA for those deployment models because customer data is isolated and encryption/keys can be managed by the customer.
- Hosted: possible in narrow cases if PHI is pseudonymized before leaving the customer environment or if guaranteed routing to a dedicated tenant is available; otherwise we recommend Dedicated/Private.

2) Evidence we will provide with the SIG/SOC2 bundle
- SOC 2 Type II summary + auditor report excerpts (redacted)
- DPA template and SCC mapping table (showing data exporter/importer flow)
- Network and encryption architecture diagram (calls out data at rest/in transit, KMS integrations)
- Data residency configuration options and region map (how requests can be routed to US/EU regions)
- For BAA path: process controls for access, incident response SLAs, and a draft BAA for redline
3) Quick clarifying questions that affect feasibility and timeline:
- Will MedSpace send raw PHI (e.g., full notes, MRN, DOB) to Redwood, or will you pseudonymize prior to sending?
- Do you require EU data to remain within EU cloud regions at all times (data residency + no export)?

If you expect raw PHI in the pilot and need EU-only residency, our Private on-prem option will be the cleanest path and usually adds 6-8 weeks for deployment + contract negotiation. Dedicated can be faster (3-6 weeks) depending on capacity.

I will attach the SIG answers and evidence bundle separately — Vanessa, please add any commercial notes for the deal.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

- Pilot plan: we will send limited PHI (structured identifiers + short clinical snippets) during the pilot. Full notes may come later in production.
- Residency: EU subject data must remain in EU regions; US subject data should remain in US regions. We do need contractual commitments on SCCs for cross-border transfers for EU->US fallback.

Attachments: I've added a short data-flow diagram for the pilot (Use-case-data-flow.pdf).
